title: Victim in fatal B.C. RCMP shooting ID'd
article: Police have identified the man shot and killed by RCMP officers in Kamloops, B.C., last week.
He has been identified as Wilbert Douglas Bartley, 50, of no fixed address. An autopsy completed Wednesday indicates he died of a gunshot wound.
Bartley was shot and killed on July 30 during a confrontation with two Mounties.
Investigators with the Calgary Police Service, brought in to investigate Bartley's death, have interviewed more than a dozen witnesses.
Officers have confirmed an unmarked RCMP minivan was behind an SUV parked near a convenience store.
Police say the SUV reversed and rammed the unmarked police car.
The two plainclothes officers, who were outside their car at the time, fired two shots into the SUV's windshield, hitting the driver once.
The SUV then continued forward and crashed into a business.
Police have not said why the two plainclothes officers were investigating Bartley.
The victim's mother, Catherine Bartley of Owen Sound, Ont., has acknowledged her son had a "lengthy" criminal record, but she has insisted he wasn't a violent man.

The two Mounties involved in the incident were put on desk duty. They have both retained lawyers, and Calgary police investigators say they expect to receive formal statements from the officers in the coming days.
The Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP has been notified.
